Authorization Tokens obtained from v1 Api by default have scope:
all
This means, if you are using v1 auth, you can ignore scope requirements, for now.
But, eventually v1 login endpoint would be removed in favor of OAuth2.0 system.

General

Web socket server address:
wss://ws.warframe.market/socket

Version

Documentation describes:
v0.12.4

Protocol

Our sockets are using
wfm
sub-protocol, do not forget to set it while establishing your connection, otherwise your connection would be dropped. Example
socket = new WebSocket('wss://ws.warframe.market/socket', 'wfm');
​
We are passing JSON-encoded messages.
Message Structure
{ route: "string" payload: any, id: "string", refId: "id" }
​
Where:
route
– Indicates which part of the application should handle this message. The application should implement a routing system that maps the
route
value to the appropriate handler.
payload
– Arbitrary data. This can be a JSON object, string, byte array, or anything else, depending on the expectations of the target handler. You can think of it as a “sub-message” or a route-specific request.
id
– A unique identifier for this message (either incoming or outgoing).
refId
– A reference to the
id
of another message. This field is used when sending a response to a previous message. It acts as a correlation ID.

Messages

Types

Somewhat abstract separation of messages, but separation nevertheless
Command ​
A request that expects a response, typically an
ok
or an
error
. Used for RPC-style interactions where acknowledgment or a result is required.
Event ​
A one-way message that does not expect a response. Used to broadcast information or signal something has happened.
Stream ​
A bidirectional flow of messages. Relies heavily on
id
and
refId
for message correlation. Often used for continuous data exchange and state synchronization.

Color codes

In this documentation i am going to highlights some parts with different colors:
Field is optional
Field required
or
Always present
Incoming message
Outgoing message

Modules

Reports

Online count ​

Once in 30 sec, server will report number of connections and number of authorized users.
◀ Incoming Message
{ "route": "@wfm|event/reports/online", "payload": { "connections": 1, "authorizedUsers": 1 } }
​

User and authorization

Sign In ​

To use most commands, your client needs to be authorized. This command supports auth tokens from the v1 API.
If, for some reason, you're still using cookie-based authorization and can’t switch just yet, set the token to an empty string, the server will attempt to read it from the cookie. (But seriously, try to migrate away from that approach)
▶ Outgoing Message
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/auth/signIn", "payload": { "token": "jwtToken" } }
​
◀ On Success
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/auth/signIn:ok", }
​
On successful Sign-In, in the next message from the server, you will receive your current online status, check Status and activity update
◀ On Error
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/auth/signIn:error", "payload": "app.error.whatever" }
​

Sign out ​

We have sign in, therefore we have sign out
▶ Outgoing Message
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/auth/signOut", }
​
◀ On Success
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/auth/signOut:ok", }
​
◀ On Error
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/auth/signOut:error", "payload": "app.error.whatever" }
​

Revoke ​

The server may revoke your session and send an event to the client. This can happen for a variety of reasons. For example, the user logs out from all devices, changes their password, or the auth token expires.
◀ Incoming Message
{ { "route": "@wfm|event/auth/revoked", "payload": { "reason": "whatever" } }
​

Verification update ​

When our bot verifies a user’s account and assigns them a name, we send this message to all of the user’s connected clients.
◀ Incoming Message
{ "route": "@wfm|event/account/verification", "payload": { "ingameName": "name", "platform": "pc", "verification": true, } }
​

Banned ​

If a moderator bans a user account, all of the user’s connected clients will receive this message.
◀ Incoming Message
{ "route": "@wfm|event/account/banned", "payload": { "banMessage": "You're a bad person", "banUntil": "2074-01-17T00:00:00Z" } }
​

Warned ​

If a moderator warns a user, all of the user’s connected clients will receive this message.
◀ Incoming Message
{ "route": "@wfm|event/account/warned", "payload": { "warnMessage": "Do not do this again" } }
​

Ban lifted ​

If a moderator lifts a user’s ban, all of the user’s connected clients will receive this message.
◀ Incoming Message
{ "route": "@wfm|event/account/banLifted", }
​

Warning lifted ​

If a warning is lifted by a moderator or acknowledged by the user, all of the user’s connected clients will receive this message.
◀ Incoming Message
{ "route": "@wfm|event/account/warningLifted", }
​

Set status and activity ​

Requires:
Authentication
Scopes:
status
,
activity
This command is used to update a user’s status and activity.
You can only update the activity if your client has been granted the
activity
scope by both WFM and the User.
How to properly set user status
Keep in mind that the server is the source of truth for a user’s online status. The server will inform your application of the user’s current status. Your app should wait for this information before deciding what to do next.
Always assume that there may be multiple clients connected to the WebSocket server simultaneously—such as a mobile app, web app, Discord bot, etc.
Because of this, never send status commands blindly, and never override a user’s status without context.
▶ Outgoing Message
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/status/set", "payload": { "status": "ingame", "duration": 1800, "activity": { "type": "onMission", "details": "Plains of Eidolon, bla bla", "startedAt": 1745424871 } } }
​
Where:
status
string - one of
online
,
ingame
,
invisible
(yes, no
offline
)
duration
int | null - for how long, in seconds, your status should be set (min 60 s, max 6 hrs)
activity
object | null - current activity of the user
type
string - one of
UNKNOWN
,
IDLE
,
ON_MISSION
,
IN_DOJO
,
IN_ORBITER
,
IN_RELAY
details
string - any optional details about current user activity, 64 char max
startedAt
int - Unix time of when activity started, should be between 1 day ago and now.
◀ On Success
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/status/set:ok", "payload": { "status": "ingame", "statusSetAt": "2017-01-16T23:00:00Z", "statusUntil": "2017-01-17T00:00:00Z", "activity": { "type": "ON_MISSION", "details": "Plains of Eidolon - Bounty Tier 3", "startedAt": "2017-01-16T23:00:00Z" } } }
For fields description check Status and activity update
ALT
​
◀ On Error
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/status/set:error", "payload": "app.error.whatever" }
​
How duration works
Let's explain this using a few scenarios:
No prior status, no duration. If you don’t have any prior status set and send a status without a duration, your status will remain active as long as you stay connected to the server.
No prior status, with duration (e.g., 180 seconds). If you send a status with a duration, your status will remain active for 180 seconds. After that, the server will set your status to
invisible
and notify all clients, if you still have active connections. If you disconnect before the 180 seconds expire, your status will still be valid for 180 seconds, after which the server will set it to
offline
.
Previously set a status with duration, now want to update status only. If you want to change your status (e.g., from
ingame
to
online
) without changing the duration, send the command without the duration field.
Previously set a status with duration, now want to remove the duration. If you want to keep your status but remove the duration, send the command with duration set to
null
.
Previously set a status without duration, now want to add one: To add a duration, send the command with the duration field set to the desired value.
In other words, it’s PATCH, with status as required field, and
duration
as nullable optional field.
How activity works
Now that you're familiar with how duration works, you can assume the
activity
field behaves similarly, and you'd be mostly right.
However, this applies only to the
activity
field as a whole, not to the contents of the
activity
object. For example, if you want to update the
activity.description
, you must also include all other fields (
type
,
startedAt
) in the same request. You cannot partially update the
activity
object—you must either replace the entire object or nullify it.

Status and activity update ​

If one of the user’s connected WebSocket clients changes their status or activity, the server sends this message to all other clients to reflect the change.
Additionally, the server is the source of truth for a user’s online status. So if your account is verified, you’ll receive this message right after logging in.
◀ Incoming Message
{ "route": "@wfm|event/status/set", "payload": { "status": "ingame", "statusSetAt": "2017-01-16T23:00:00Z", "statusUntil": "2017-01-17T00:00:00Z", "activity": { "type": "ON_MISSION", "details": "Plains of Eidolon - Bounty Tier 3", "startedAt": "2017-01-16T23:00:00Z" } } }
​
Where:
status
string - one of
offline
,
online
,
ingame
statusUntil
string - point of no return, at this time your status will be set as
offline
or
invisible
activity
object - current activity of the user
type
string - one of
UNKNOWN
,
IDLE
,
ON_MISSION
,
IN_DOJO
,
IN_ORBITER
,
IN_RELAY
details
string - any optional details about current user activity, 64 char max
startedAt
string - When the activity was started

Order subscriptions

Subscribe to new orders ​

Use this subscription to receive a live feed of the most recent orders. It subscribes the client to newly posted orders from users who are either Online or Online in Game.
▶ Outgoing Message
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/subscribe/newOrders", "payload": { "platform": "pc", "crossplay": true } }
​
Where:
platform
string - one of
pc
,
ps4
,
xbox
,
switch
,
mobile
If not set, you will receive orders from
all
platforms.
crossplay
bool - Whether to include orders from other platforms if those orders have cross-play enabled. if not set, the default will be
true
The
switch
platform cannot have
crossplay: true
. It will automatically be assigned
false
.
You can have multiple subscriptions active at the same time (e.g., one for
pc
, one for
xbox
).
◀ On Success
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/subscribe/newOrders:ok", }
​
◀ On Error
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/subscribe/newOrders:error", "payload": "app.error.whatever" }
​

Unsubscribe from new orders ​

Unsubscribes the client from receiving newly posted orders. You must provide the exact same payload that was used during subscription. This is necessary because multiple subscriptions can be active simultaneously.
▶ Outgoing Message
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/unsubscribe/newOrders", "payload": { "platform": "pc", "crossplay": true } }
​
Where:
platform
string - one of
pc
,
ps4
,
xbox
,
switch
,
mobile
If not set, you will unsubscribe from
all
platforms, only if you previously have sub to
all
platforms. If you have sub for
all
and
xbox
not setting platform will only unsubscribe you from
all
.
crossplay
bool - Whether to include orders from other platforms if those orders have cross-play enabled. if not set, default will be
true
The
switch
platform cannot have
crossplay: true
. It will automatically be set to
false
.
◀ On Success
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/unsubscribe/newOrders:ok", }
​
◀ On Error
{ "route": "@wfm|cmd/unsubscribe/newOrders:error", "payload": "app.error.whatever" }
​
